name: 登录 / 两标签注销与重新登录 / 旧 Cookie 和登录 Bearer 均撤销，深链恢复
identity: admin browser; separate cookie-only and bearer-only clients
phase_zero: Cookie and returned login Bearer bind to the same revocable management session. Logout removes that session; storage events notify the second tab. Re-authentication retains each deep link. No token refresh, idle expiry or GPU behavior is claimed.

fields.persistence: authenticated user identity; not a user creation operation
N/A: supplied credential is verified; not saved as a new password

covered: Both languages are chosen through the login page's own dropdown: the trigger is clicked, the menu item is clicked by its literal name, and the trigger's compact text must become the expected marker (EN, 中文) - so a run that only sets --locale never satisfies this. The selection is then read back two ways: the trigger text after reload proves the choice survives a full page load (localStorage gpuworks.locale), and reopening the dropdown shows the item carrying ant-dropdown-menu-item-selected, which is the control's own idea of the current choice rather than an inference from the page language. The session is returned to the run's locale at the end. Proven by mutation: setting caches: [] in ui/src/i18n/index.ts fails with 'expected 中文, actual EN' after the reload.

missing: MISSING: initial session-check failure and authenticated check failure show retry and recover via the real server; logout-failure coverage remains separately missing

covered: named dialog in viewport after peer logout
Enter submits valid credentials and restores both deep links
missing: MISSING: Esc and mask cannot dismiss mandatory reauthentication; default focus, Tab/Shift+Tab containment
MISSING: empty/wrong credentials and correction in this modal while both tabs remain unauthenticated

checklist_items.1.1: On first open the login form shows an empty username textbox whose autocomplete is username and an empty password field whose type is password and whose autocomplete is current-password. Neither field has a maximum length. There is no spinbutton. Both fields are visible together. Submitting them empty shows the username-required and password-required messages and sends no login POST. The later login POST sends username admin and the password. The login response contains token and user. That user and the independent GET /api/v1/auth/me contain id, username admin, and role admin, and do not contain a password.
checklist_items.1.7: Signing in fills only the two required fields. The username textbox and the password field are large inputs. The sign-in POST to /api/v1/auth/login sends username admin and the password, and the 200 response keys are token and user. The user has id, username admin, and role admin, and it does not contain a password. The response is that one user, not a list of sessions. Reloading the networks page shows the networks heading, and the independent GET /api/v1/auth/me returns that same user.
checklist_items.1.10: A real server refusal is asserted end to end, not simulated. A wrong credential answers 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS with the exact body, the form keeps both values the operator typed, the translated alert is required to be visible, no session cookie may be created, and an independent client is required to still be anonymous afterwards. Clearing the alert on the next keystroke is asserted, so the failure is readable and recoverable without a reload.
checklist_items.1.14: After login, re-entering the networks page shows the networks heading and no password field, and that page agrees with an independent GET /api/v1/auth/me of the saved identity. A direct settings deep link, refreshed again, shows the settings heading and the same identity. Cookie-only and bearer-only clients both read that identity. This management session attaches no agent or workload.
checklist_items.1.9: A sign-in in flight cannot be doubled. The login request is held open at the network layer, the form is required to stay in flight with exactly one request on the wire, and a second click plus Enter are then both issued while it is held - the request count is required to still be one, and the single request that is released is required to carry the intended body and no query string. The assertion is on the request count before the visual busy state, so the case fails on the contract rather than on the class that happens to enforce it, and the busy state is still asserted afterwards so the reason a duplicate cannot get through is visible. Only one session is created by the exchange, which the identity checks that follow confirm. Proven by mutation: rendering the button busy without disabling it makes the second click produce a second request and the case fails on the request count.

not_applicable.7.3: Login bearer is returned to API clients, not displayed as a one-time UI credential

checklist_items.22.1: covered: The sidebar the page actually renders is enumerated at runtime rather than read from the route table, and all 19 entries are entered by deep link. For each one the case asserts the address it settles on (a child route such as /analytics/usage is accepted only when it sits under that entry), that exactly one menu entry highlights and it is the expected one, that the page renders a non-empty heading, and that a reload keeps both the address and the highlighted entry. The settled path, the heading and whether the heading happens to equal the menu label are recorded per entry.
checklist_items.22.5: covered for the navigation surface, which is what this case owns: the same 19 entries were run in en and in zh and every heading differs between the two runs - Overview/概览, Monitor Center/监控中心, Usage analytics/用量分析, Public Clouds/公有云, Private Clouds/专有云, Nodes/计算节点, GPU Devices/GPU 设备, Model Repository/模型仓库, Inference Templates/推理模板, Images/镜像, Storage/存储, Networks/网络, Deploy/部署, Deployments/部署列表, Playground/试验场, Evaluations/评测, API Tokens/API 令牌, Logs/日志, Settings/设置. This is the navigation entry and first-screen title, not a full-page language audit of every form, error and empty state; those stay with the cases that own those surfaces.
checklist_items.1.2: The opening state of both fields is asserted before anything is typed: the username box and the password field both read empty on a first visit, so the form does not open pre-filled with a previous or default identity. The three later clauses of this item do not apply to a sign-in form and are not claimed here: there is no edit mode and so no saved value to refill, there is no asynchronous load whose completion has to gate submission, and the credential is the operator's own password, which the product never has occasion to read back and which is asserted elsewhere to stay unmasked only as input type.
checklist_items.1.6: N/A: this form has no conditional control. Neither field is shown or hidden by another control, there is no value withheld from a submission because its switch is off, and there is no reveal-then-hide sequence to check for retention, so nothing of this item applies and no such control is invented for a two-field sign-in form.
checklist_items.1.8: N/A: there are no optional fields. The form has exactly the two fields a sign-in needs, both required, so the largest possible submission is also the smallest one and there is no optional value to persist or omit for a backend default. That maximal submission is the one covered as the minimal create, so nothing here is left untested for want of a claim.
checklist_items.1.11: Dismissal is asserted where this surface has one. The language chooser is opened from the sign-in page, Escape is pressed, and the popup is required to close with the current language unchanged and no mutation on the wire - a dismissal is not a choice, so nothing may be written. Cancel and close buttons are not claimed here: this form has neither, and no unsaved-draft prompt exists to verify because the surface holds no draft across a dismissal, so nothing is invented for them.
checklist_items.1.15: Keyboard order and layout at the stated size. Tab from the first field is required to land on the password field and Shift+Tab to come back, with no stop skipped. Enter and a submit click on an incomplete form are both required to put nothing on the wire, and the required message for the field that was left blank is required to be visible, so a keyboard submit cannot silently do nothing. At 1440x900 both fields and the submit button are required to be inside the viewport with non-zero size and to be ordered top to bottom without overlap, which is asserted from their measured boxes rather than from styles. This entry is not mutation-proven: the tab order and the Enter behaviour are the widget library's own, the page has no code of its own to break for them, and an attempt to push the submit button over the fields did not move it because the wrapper owns the layout - that attempt is not offered as evidence.
checklist_items.1.3: Both required fields are exercised in both forbidden shapes, per field. Empty: submitting an untouched form is required to show both required messages and to put no request on the wire. Whitespace only: submitting spaces alone is likewise required to show both messages, to keep the typed text in the field, and to send nothing, because a value that trims to nothing is not a value. The message is asserted on the operator's screen next to the field it belongs to rather than as a banner, so the error is located at the field that caused it.
checklist_items.7.1: covered: both credential fields are treated by their own contract rather than assumed required. Each field is exercised empty and whitespace-only and required to show its own message inside its own form item, so a message that merely appears somewhere on the page is not accepted, and an empty submit is required to send no request at all. The password is required to be masked on input, and the mask is then traversed as a state: the value stays masked while the toggle is untouched, one activation is required to make it readable with the characters unchanged, a second is required to mask it again with the characters still unchanged, and the toggle is required to exist exactly once, so a control that only redrew its icon, or one that dropped the value, fails here. Proven by mutation: replacing the password input with a plain one fails as the type is text where a mask is required.
checklist_items.22.6: covered: the focus and disabled states are read from the browser's computed style instead of from the presence of a class, and the reading is taken on a field reached by keyboard in its normal state. The wrapper's shadow is required to be stronger when the field is focused than when it is blurred - both its alpha and its spread must grow - rather than merely different, because this theme animates the ring in from a faint trace and a difference-only check would be satisfied by that residue. The numbers are recorded: focused alpha 0.925 at 1.85px against blurred 0.047 at 0.09px. The submit button's colour, cursor and background are read too, and its own disabled flag is recorded as false, because this form never disables its submit - an empty submit is refused by validation instead - so no disabled-state claim is made for it. Proven by mutation: making the primary soft colour transparent fails with both strengths printed. Tab order, Enter behaviour and the 1440x900 geometry remain asserted separately by the same case.
checklist_items.7.4: covered: A freshly minted management credential performs real allowed operations (GET /api/v1/auth/me, /api/v1/models, /api/v1/nodes, /api/v1/storages all 200), then the session reaches its inactivity deadline and every one of the same four operations returns 401 with the product's AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED body, read back through an independent transport carrying only that credential. Expiry is reached for real: the isolated server runs the product's own session_idle_timeout from server.yaml, because the shipped default in auth.SessionPolicy.Normalized is 24h. A management token's own expires_in_days is a whole-day field whose minimum is therefore unreachable inside a test window, so the session credential - which is what every management call actually carries - is the credential driven to expiry. Incorrect password and explicit revocation remain asserted as before. Mutation-proven: ignoring the idle deadline in the session lookup makes the four post-expiry operations return 200 instead of 401, which fails the expiry assertion.
checklist_items.7.6: covered: Nine download, export and log surfaces are really fetched over an independent transport with no cookie jar - /telemetry/export, /usage-report, /usage-report/preview, /experience, /analytics/key-usage, /logs/search, /logs/histogram, /platform-tokens and /data-retention/status - and each must answer 200 with a non-empty body, so a surface that is unreachable or silently empty cannot pass by being absent. Every response body is searched for a live freshly minted management token in its raw, JSON-escaped and base64 forms. The server's own log file is scanned as well: it must contain the token-creation record, which keeps the absence check from passing on an empty log, while the live token itself must not appear there. This is complementary to the provider declaration, which covers raw provider list/detail GETs and the upstream error path into WARN/logstore plus a source audit for credential download/export; this covers the file and export surfaces that hand bytes back to the caller, which the provider row does not reach. Mutation-proven: logging the full token instead of its prefix makes the log scan report the credential in cleartext.
checklist_items.22.4: covered: Logging out and re-authenticating keeps the destination page, and a login dies of inactivity without being kept alive by background polling. A cookie-only transport polls GET /api/v1/auth/me continuously past the inactivity deadline; it answers 200 four times and then 401 for the rest of the run, which is a direct observation that a passive GET poll cannot renew the session (the product renews only on non-GET, api.managementAuth). Once the product observes that 401 it raises its own re-authentication dialog. An unsaved settings form survives all of it: the draft is still readable after the login has expired but before the tab has noticed, still readable under the dialog, and still readable after re-authenticating through that dialog, with the expired cookie staying 401 and the replacement cookie reading the same identity at the original deep link. Mutation-proven twice: renewing on GET too makes the poll answer 200 throughout, and unmounting SessionBoundary's children while expired loses the draft.

response_observation: Chrome response-stage barrier is limited to exact login/logout POST. Fetch.getResponseBody reads actual server bytes; Fetch.continueResponse supplies only requestId.
